tests.name: LevelControl MoveToLevel verification on DimmableLight
tests.comment: Deterministically fails at Step 5h (3/3 reproductions): after OnOff.Off then MoveToLevel with Options.ExecuteIfOff=0, CurrentLevel should stay unchanged (120 sent, expects level to remain at the prior 100) but reads back as 120 instead. LevelControlServer's own #optionsAllowExecution() check (@matter/node, not Matterbridge code) reads the live OnOffServer OnOff attribute and correctly blocks execution — verified manually replaying the exact same command sequence one chip-tool process at a time (fresh CASE session per command), where the block works every time. Only reproduces inside chiptool.py's single long-lived interactive-server session sending the Off and MoveToLevel commands back-to-back, suggesting a race between the Off command's state commit and the following MoveToLevel's OnOff read under low-latency/pipelined command delivery — needs deeper investigation in @matter/node before enabling. Re-verified unchanged after removing the OnOff/LevelControl forwarder await under MATTERBRIDGE_CHIP_TEST (packages/core/src/behaviors/onOffServer.ts / levelControlServer.ts) and after opting LevelControl into managedTransitionTimeHandling: still fails identically, confirming the race is inside @matter/node's own OnOff/LevelControl state handling, not the Matterbridge forwarder or the transition-time gap.

tests.name: ColorControl StopMoveStep functionality on ExtendedColorLightEnhancedEHSXYCT
tests.note: Exercises Stop (primary focus) across HS, CT and EHUE in-progress Move/MoveTo operations, plus the generic StopMoveStep command itself.
tests.comment: The managedTransitionTimeHandling opt-in under MATTERBRIDGE_CHIP_TEST (packages/core/src/behaviors/colorControlServer.ts) fixed this test's original failure (step 9, HS Stop) and the CT/HS Stop sections that follow — the test now progresses from 10 successes/1 error to 60 successes/1 error. It still fails at step 37 (Step 5e, the EnhancedMoveHue section, second read 10s after Stop): StopMoveStep genuinely never stops an EnhancedCurrentHue transition on any Matterbridge ColorControl endpoint, because @matter/node's ColorControlServer.stopMoveStepLogic() only calls transitions.stop('enhancedCurrentHue') when 'this.state.colorLoopActive === ColorControl.ColorLoopActive.Inactive' (0) — but colorLoopActive is undefined (not 0) whenever the ColorLoop feature isn't included, which is every Matterbridge ColorControl endpoint (no createXxxColorControlClusterServer() helper enables ColorLoop), so the strict-equality guard is always false and the stop call is always skipped. Verified directly against the container with an isolated repro script: EnhancedCurrentHue keeps climbing at the full commanded rate for at least 10s after StopMoveStep is sent and acknowledged. This is a genuine @matter/node bug (an edge case the library's own guard doesn't account for), not Matterbridge code; needs a fix or workaround upstream before enabling.
